title: Observation only: the flagged wal_wait is a single-backend wait below the storage noise floor, while GetUserTweets consumes 87.87% of terminal capacity
configuration_cause: No incumbent storage setting is causally implicated by the measured evidence. The only settings that could generate the flagged wal_wait are the durability pipeline: wal_sync_method=open_datasync, wal_writer_delay=215 ms, wal_writer_flush_after=367 pages, wal_buffers=637 pages, commit_delay=671 us with commit_siblings=12. Their own telemetry refutes queueing on that path (wal_write_time_per_txn=9.65e-4 ms, wal_sync_time_per_txn=0.0, wal_timing.write_average_ms=0.134, host_io some/full stall fraction=0.0, wal_waiting_backends median=0/p95=0/max=1 out of ~9 backends). commit_delay is moreover inert at this concurrency: it arms only when at least commit_siblings=12 other sessions are in active transactions, and numbackends peaks at 10 (active max 9). shared_buffers=53504 pages (~418 MB) with buffer_hit_ratio=0.999921 and 7.30e-4 blks_read per transaction shows no cache shortfall, and temp_files=temp_bytes=0 rules out spill. Checkpoint/bgwriter are idle, not misconfigured for this load: checkpoints_req=0, checkpoint_write_time=0, checkpoint_sync_time=0, buffers_clean=0.0/s, buffers_checkpoint_per_txn=2.36e-4.
mechanism: Storage demand in this incumbent is two to four orders of magnitude below device capacity, so the storage layer cannot be the rate limiter. WAL generation is 152.1 kB/s, i.e. 4.77 bytes and 0.0072 WAL writes per transaction; WAL write service time is 0.134 ms per write and 9.65e-4 ms per transaction (about 1e-5 % of wall time per transaction), and no backend ever recorded an fsync (wal_sync=0.0/s, wal_sync_time=0.0, wal_timing.sync_average_ms=null). The buffer path is equally idle: 9.28 buffer hits per transaction at a 0.999921 hit ratio, 7.30e-4 block reads per transaction, and blk_read_time_per_txn=6.65e-6 ms. Writeback is quiescent: buffers_clean=0.0/s, dirty_bytes median 4.28 MB / p95 33.0 MB, writeback_bytes median 0, PSI some/full I/O stall fraction 0.0, io_waiting_backends max 1, wal_waiting_backends max 1. A single instantaneous WALWrite wait on at most one of ~9 backends across 154 samples is below the queueing/sampling noise floor of an 8-terminal closed loop. Meanwhile the client side is the binding resource: GetUserTweets alone consumes 0.8787 of terminal capacity (843.50 s of 8 x 168.44 s = 1347.54 s) at a 157 us median / 244.5 us mean / 593 us p95, and the sum of all transaction-class fractions is ~0.996, i.e. the eight terminals are effectively 100% busy. In a saturation-limited closed loop, throughput equals terminals/latency, so only reductions in client-observed per-transaction latency can raise TPS, and the storage share of that latency is ~1e-6 to 1e-3 ms per transaction. The multi-millisecond tails (GetUserTweets max 27.2 ms, GetTweetsFromFollowing max 31.5 ms, InsertTweet max 54.9 ms) appear across read-only and write classes alike and coincide with zero PSI stall and zero checkpoint write/sync time, so they are not explained by storage service time.

intermediate_metrics.aggregation: mean per transaction over 168.44 s (sync_average_ms reported as null: no sync event recorded)

query_effect: None. The read path already resolves through shared buffers (EXPLAIN plan evidence: Index Scan on tweets id=1, uses_index=true, estimated_rows=1) at a 0.999921 hit ratio with 9.28 buffer hits per transaction; no plan or access-path change is available inside the storage domain.
expected_tps_effect: None from this domain. With storage service time per transaction between ~1e-6 ms (block reads) and ~1e-3 ms (WAL writes), and the eight terminals ~99.6% busy, no permitted storage knob can move the incumbent's 31906.7 rps in the next round.
expected_latency_effect: None attributable to storage. The 157 us p50 / 244.5 us mean of GetUserTweets is parse, plan, buffer access and round-trip; the storage component is less than 0.001% of that latency. InsertTweet's p99 of 3336 us is likewise not sync-dominated, since wal_sync_time is zero and host I/O stalls are zero.

predictions.rationale: The class consumes 0.8787 of terminal capacity (843.50 s of 1347.54 s) at a 157 us median while its storage cost is ~6.65e-6 ms of block read time and zero temp bytes; no storage knob in the allowed set can shift this fraction by 3 points.

Observed 9.65e-4 ms per transaction with write_average_ms=0.134 and PSI io stall fraction 0.0; the WAL write path has no queue to relieve, so no storage-side reconfiguration should change it by more than 25%.

The flagged wait is a single instantaneous sample: median 0.0, p95 0.0, max 1 out of ~9 backends. Reconfiguring the WAL/commit pipeline cannot remove a wait that is not present beyond the noise floor, so the max should not move by 1 or more backends.

InsertTweet p99 is 3336 us on 0.0072 WAL writes and zero recorded fsync time per transaction; the commit durability path is not the tail driver, so its p99 should not move by 10% from any permitted storage change.

alternatives.statement: A slow durable flush (fsync/open_datasync) on the commit path inflates InsertTweet's tail and forces backends to queue on WAL.
Background-writer or checkpoint writeback bursts stall readers and produce the 17-31 ms maxima seen across read-only classes.
shared_buffers is too small for the twitter working set, so the read path pays buffer misses that dominate GetUserTweets latency.

cross_domain_requirements: query_execution: attribute the 244.5 us GetUserTweets mean and 2280 us p99 to parse/plan/round-trip cost, since storage contributes <0.001% of per-transaction latency here.
concurrency_maintenance: with eight terminals ~99.6% busy, validate the terminal/admission model before any server-side micro-tuning; throughput is terminal-time-bound, not resource-bound.
measurement: keep track_io_timing and track_wal_io_timing enabled so wal_timing and host_io evidence remain available to falsify any storage hypothesis in the next round.
why_exceeds_incumbent: It does not claim a TPS gain; it claims the incumbent storage configuration is already non-binding and left untouched, which strictly dominates any unfalsifiable storage edit. Every storage path shows >=99.9% idle headroom: wal_write_time_per_txn 9.65e-4 ms, wal_sync_time_per_txn 0, blk_read_time_per_txn 6.65e-6 ms, checkpoint write+sync time 0, buffers_clean 0/s, PSI full/some io stall 0.0, temp_bytes 0. Acting on the wal_wait alert would spend measurement budget on a no-op while risking a real regression (e.g. enlarging wal_buffers/shared_buffers at 418 MB with a 0.999921 hit ratio, or trading commit-path latency for a group-commit benefit that cannot materialise because commit_delay needs >=12 concurrent sibling transactions and only ~9 backends exist).
